text:
24-hour news summary

1 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5740) A researcher argues that science may soon benefit from combining existing ideas more efficiently, as mathematics has begun to do.
2 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5741) Google Research announced a randomized trial examining AI’s effects on patent attorneys’ productivity and long-term expertise.
3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5742) A post argues that AI performs especially well in mathematics because it can be precisely formalized and verified, unlike many aspects of medical research.
4 ProjectDiscovery demonstrated that hiding a backdoor in an open model can cost less than $50 using a small LoRA fine-tune.
5 A Stanford paper reports that the decentralized DeLM multi-agent system outperformed Claude Code and Codex on complex coding tasks, with speeds up to 2.49 times faster.
6 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5745) A post warns that OpenAI’s claimed Navier–Stokes solution does not match its Lean verification, highlighting limits of relying on formal proof checks.
7 A researcher criticizes treating mathematical proofs like software that can be patched after release.
8 Honen launched an AI-era workforce training platform and announced an NVIDIA partnership targeting 250,000 learners.
9 Neuphonic released NeuDecide, a 43 MB offline audio decision model that converts speech directly into tool calls.
10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5750) Arena announced a $200 million Series B at a $3.1 billion valuation and introduced its AI Alignment Index.
11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5751) The Financial Times reported that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion, below earlier estimates of $70 billion.
12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5752) A satirical post claims that President Trump considers people who use the term “Artificial Intelligence” to be enemies.
13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5753) Odyssey released Odyssey-3, an autoregressive world model whose Pro version reportedly achieved a leading Physics-IQ Verified video-to-video score.
14 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5754) OpenAI began rolling out Ultrafast for GPT-6.1 Sol, promising near-Astra intelligence at up to eight times Sol Standard’s speed.
15 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5755) OpenCode made Step 5 Preview free for a week, including a one-million-token context window, multimodal support, and zero data retention.
16 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5756) Artificial Analysis announced that its Intelligence Index v5 will launch in late October with new science and private-dataset coding benchmarks.
17 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5757) Anthropic’s proposed usage policy may prohibit sustained and needless abusive behavior toward Claude.
18 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5758) Former OpenAI safety researchers said they were fired after prioritizing safety over the company’s near-term corporate interests.
19 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5759) CrowdStrike reported that one person may have conducted a major South Korean banking cyberattack using several AI-assisted security tools and models.
20 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5760) Anthropic introduced beta versions of Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion for creating live data dashboards and animated explainers.
21 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5761) SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide portfolio of low-band spectrum licenses to help Starlink become a major US mobile carrier.
22 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5762) An astrophysicist used Claude Science to create the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky.
23 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5763) Claude Max subscribers now receive monthly API credits, enabling projects such as an automatically generated AI homepage.
24 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5764) A proposal argues that AI personal assistants should focus less on leisure planning and more on helping Americans address the cost of living.
25 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5765) A post notes that every recipient of the nation’s top scientific award is a foreign-born immigrant. (1/2)
